column1: # Conditional fn-shadow (found by the variation sweep, forward-barrier.tsv:73;
# fixed to a SOUND REFUSAL the same day). A user fn REDEFINED inside a
# conditionally-reached body — an if/case arm or a for/each loop body —
# overlap-removes the enclosing overload IN PLACE (installDef drops the outer
# entry then pushes the new one at the SAME def depth), so the branch/loop def
# rollback (which restores by depth GROWTH) cannot revert it. Compiled
# resolution then statically bakes the conditional shadow, while the
# interpreter keeps the outer fn when the branch is NOT taken (or the loop runs
# zero times) — `if false [def g …] g 1` returned the shadow's value compiled
# but the ORIGINAL interpreted. The fix refuses to compile the redefinition
# (CondBodyDepth-gated, eng/go/core_helpers.go), so the interpreter owns the
# shape with full parity. Full graduation = a runtime dispatch that respects
# the conditional binding compiles these rows, at which point the entries in
# frontierCompileLedger delete and the rows move to the main corpus.
def g fn [[x:Any] [Integer] [x add 100]] if false [def g fn [[x:Any] [Integer] [x add 1]]] g 1
